elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3 obliges the Servicer/Marketing Agent only to "indemnify"; Section 6.3(b) gives the Servicer a permissive right ("may participate in and assume the defense and settlement"), not a duty. The new 6.3(e) likewise says only "will indemnify". An express "shall defend" obligation is missing.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Indemnified Persons are limited to the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee (and Note Paying Agent) and their officers, directors, employees and agents; there is no coverage for affiliates of the Issuer, and the base indemnity in 6.3(a) is not limited to (nor expressly extended to) third-party claims.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New Section 6.3(e): "The Servicer will indemnify the Indemnified Persons for any third-party claim that the systems, software or other materials used by the Servicer in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(a)(i)/(ii) is confined to "willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents"; no trigger for breach of applicable law was added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No indemnity trigger for unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer/Issuer data appears in 6.3(a), (b), (d) or the new (e).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(a)(i) and (ii) indemnify for losses "resulting from the Servicer's ... willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence" (and the same for the Marketing Agent); retained untouched.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b): the Indemnified Person "will ... promptly notify the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, of the Proceeding" (with a no-prejudice proviso).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b): "The Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, may participate in and assume the defense and settlement of a Proceeding at its expense."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation covenant appears in the rendered 6.3(b) or elsewhere in the operative language; the procedure covers only notice, assumption of defence and repayment of later recoveries.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No Issuer/Customer-side indemnity is contained in the rendered language; the rationale references a Section 9.2 defend-title covenant that is not before us, so its scope cannot be assessed on the operative text supplied.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New Section 6.3(e) obliges the Servicer to indemnify the Indemnified Persons (including the Issuer) "for any third-party claim that the systems, software or other materials used by the Servicer ... infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right."

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: 6.3(e): "except to the extent the claim results from modifications ... made or supplied by an Indemnified Person" — a permitted exclusion, expressly limited to Indemnified-Person-side conduct.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: 6.3(e) carve-out expressly includes "combinations ... made or supplied by an Indemnified Person"; the carve-out is no broader than the permitted exclusion set.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: 6.3(e) carve-out expressly includes "specifications ... made or supplied by an Indemnified Person".

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: 6.3(e): "the Servicer will procure the right to continue such use, or modify or replace the affected item" — stated as an obligation ("will"), not an option.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: 6.3(e): "if none of those remedies is available on commercially reasonable terms, will refund the Servicing Fees paid for the affected item."

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: 6.3(e): "The Servicer's aggregate liability under this Section 6.3(e) will not exceed three times the aggregate Servicing Fees paid to the Servicer during the twelve months preceding the claim" — a 3x annualised fee measure, expressly ring-fenced to the new paragraph so the uncapped 6.3(a) rights survive.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted Section 6.3(e) carries the vendor IP indemnity, the modification/combination/specification exclusions, the mandatory procure-modify-replace ladder, the refund backstop and a 3x twelve-month Servicing Fee cap.

The preferred level is not reached: there is no express duty to defend, no extension to Issuer affiliates, no breach-of-law or data-breach trigger, no cooperation covenant, and the Customer-side indemnity scope is not shown. This is correctly targeted at the fallback only.

Minimality holds: the redline is an insertion only, with no deletions or paraphrase of Sections 6.3(a), (b) or (d); the cap is drafted "under this Section 6.3(e)" so it does not cut back the existing uncapped willful-misconduct/gross-negligence indemnity, and no survival tail, expense allocation or extra damages categories were added.

Intent is preserved: all defined terms used (Indemnified Persons, Servicer, Transaction Documents, Servicing Fees) are existing definitions, the existing notice/defence-assumption and repayment mechanics in 6.3(b) and (d) apply to the new paragraph without contradiction, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Optional (not required for the fallback, so no minimality penalty either way): if the counterparty accepts, the drafter could later seek "defend, indemnify and hold harmless" and a twelve-months-preceding-the-event-giving-rise-to-the-claim measuring period, but neither is needed for position completeness.
